claims.text: The coating is a dual-phase FCC/BCC high-entropy alloy.
The initial coating has a refined microstructure with coherent FCC/BCC interfaces.
Load partitioning and dislocation locking at coherent FCC/BCC boundaries primarily govern the coating's creep resistance.
Thermal annealing can reduce the coherency and sharpness of the FCC/BCC phase boundaries.
Coherent FCC/BCC phase boundaries act as barriers to dislocation motion.
The interfaces promote load partitioning between the FCC and BCC phases.
The interfaces inhibit dislocation glide through dislocation locking.
Interface-mediated load partitioning and inhibition of dislocation glide reduce creep rate under continuous loading.
Coatings retaining coherent FCC/BCC interfaces will have a lower creep deformation rate than annealed coatings with less coherent interfaces.
The as-deposited coating will maintain its integrity longer under sustained loading than the annealed, less coherent coating.
The naturally coherent interfaces in the as-deposited coating constitute the optimal state for creep resistance.
The proposed interface-controlled mechanism operates below the temperature at which diffusional creep dominates, provisionally identified as approximately 0.4 T_m.
At higher temperatures, alternative creep mechanisms may dominate.
At stresses beyond the elastic limit, alternative creep mechanisms may dominate.
